FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: The adaptive-directive config path is operationally dead. [dynamic_management.py#L5524](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5524) loads registry `adaptive_directive` text into `self.config.per_model_directives`, [dynamic_management.py#L5537](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5537) exposes `get_model_directive()`, and [dynamic_management.py#L5640](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5640) plus [dynamic_management.py#L5738](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5738) mutate the same field as an immune remediation. But the actual dispatch paths in [run_exp17_immune.py#L1247](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1247) and [run_exp18_confer.py#L521](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp18_confer.py#L521) build prompts and call `dispatch_to_model(..., cdsfl_text)` directly, without ever reading `mgr.get_model_directive()` or `mgr.config.per_model_directives`. So a whole class of config-driven remediations reports success in manager state but never changes model inputs. This is a real control-path break, not just dead documentation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply per-model directives at the dispatch boundary, preferably by composing `cdsfl_text` with `mgr.get_model_directive(model_id)` immediately before `dispatch_to_model()`. Add a regression test that setting a directive changes the outbound system prompt for both Exp 17 and Exp 18 runners.  
VERIFIED: TRUE  

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig`’s vector invariants are bypassable after construction because the code validates temporary arrays but does not store defensive copies, then returns aliased arrays from its accessors. In [dynamic_management.py#L206](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L206), `__post_init__()` checks `vec = np.asarray(...)` for `alpha_*` only transiently. Later [dynamic_management.py#L238](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L238) and [dynamic_management.py#L247](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L247) return `np.asarray(self.alpha_*/self.b_*, dtype=np.float64)` without copying. Under the default ndarray-backed config, `np.asarray` returns the same object, so a caller can mutate `cfg.get_alpha(...)` or `cfg.get_baseline(...)` and silently alter role scoring or underperformance baselines after validation has already passed. Because these vectors feed `RoleAssignment._capability_score()` and `FailureHandler._expected_performance()`, this is a hidden post-init invariant break in core decision logic.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In `__post_init__()`, coerce and copy `alpha_*` and `b_*` back onto the dataclass (`self.alpha_pm = np.asarray(...).copy()`, etc.), and have `get_alpha()` / `get_baseline()` return copies or immutable tuples. If mutation is not intended, freeze the config or wrap vectors in read-only arrays.  
VERIFIED: TRUE  

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88  
DESCRIPTION: The config object is being used as mutable runtime state, which breaks configuration reproducibility and lets adaptive behavior bypass the manager’s own audit model. [dynamic_management.py#L4846](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4846) stores the caller’s config by reference. After that, manager internals mutate `self.config.per_model_directives` and `self.config.pre_decompose_models` in [dynamic_management.py#L5527](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5527), [dynamic_management.py#L5648](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5648), [dynamic_management.py#L5660](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5660), [dynamic_management.py#L5717](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5717), and [dynamic_management.py#L5740](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5740). The runners also mutate the same config directly at [run_exp17_immune.py#L1268](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1268), [run_exp17_immune.py#L1279](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1279), and [run_exp18_confer.py#L552](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp18_confer.py#L552). That means “config” no longer means declarative input; it becomes a mutable accumulation of runtime history. Reusing one config object across runs can leak prior adaptive state into later experiments, and external direct mutations are invisible to the manager’s damping and adjustment-log machinery.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Separate immutable configuration from adaptive runtime state. Deep-copy the config in `DynamicManager.__init__()`, move `per_model_directives` / `pre_decompose_models` into a dedicated manager-owned state object, and require all mutations to go through logged methods so damping, audit, and replay all observe the same state transitions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
